summary: Coast Guard light in Hecate Strait: an unattended beacon from 1927, a staffed steel tower from 1960, and keepers listed to 2024; reached by boat or air.

structures.note: White mast, slatted wooden ball and red lantern (LighthouseFriends).
Lantern painted red. LighthouseFriends says placed between 1982 and 1994.

staffing.note: Head keeper listed to at least 2024 (LighthouseFriends). The 2024 Coast Guard release counts 25 other staffed BC stations without naming them.

access.note: Staffed Coast Guard light station where keepers live. Reached by boat or floatplane (the LighthouseFriends author chartered a float plane out of Prince Rupert). Visitors should not land without the Coast Guard's invitation.

visit.grounds_note: LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory describe the grounds as open and the tower as closed; the station is a working post.

events.note: Preliminary expenses for a lighthouse and dwelling, reported in the fiscal year 1912-13. LighthouseFriends infers the project was dropped.
Stange Construction built three dwellings, a fog alarm building and a light tower, at a cost roughly $200,000 (LighthouseFriends).
Steel tower exhibited, flashing white light with a red sector.
The lighthouse replaced the small beacon (Lighthouse Directory).
Diaphone fog alarm, one blast every thirty seconds (LighthouseFriends).
Present round tower placed sometime between 1982 and 1994 (LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard announced plans to discontinue the foghorn (LighthouseFriends). Outcome not in sources.

keepers.name: Eric Van Rooyen
keepers.note: The year is not printed beside his name. It comes from the December 1995 Santa visit in the same LighthouseFriends article, which names him as keeper. Not in LighthouseFriends' head-keeper list.

keepers.name: Harvey Bergen
keepers.note: Called Principal Lightkeeper at Bonilla Island in the Senate committee's witness list of Friday 19 November 2010 (Prince Rupert). LighthouseFriends' list ends 2013; its text says he retired in 2012.

wrecks.outcome: Disabled with a broken tail shaft off Bonilla Island. The Newington towed her and her raft to a safe anchorage the next morning. No station role recorded.
Fire aboard; Associated Press report placed her anchored fifteen miles northwest of Bonilla Island, awaiting help. No station role recorded.

corrections.why: The Coast Guard's list gives 53 29 33.1 N, 130 38 15.0 W (LighthouseFriends gives the same to the minute). The current point is from OpenStreetMap.
The Coast Guard's list gives a red sector: white 360 to 168 degrees, red 168 to 198, obscured 198 to 334, red 334 to 360. The record omits it.
The 1927 structure was the unattended beacon. The present 10 m round tower is dated 1982 to 1994 by LighthouseFriends; the Directory gives no earlier date for it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's two first years are both right for different structures: the unattended beacon was first lit in 1927, and the steel tower was first exhibited in 1960.

The Directory describes a white or red flash depending on bearing, every 5 s; the Coast Guard list gives the same sector pattern as Fl W R 5s. The sector is part of the current characteristic, not a change.
LighthouseFriends' head-keeper list gives 1996 to 2013; its text says he retired in 2012. The story states both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence: two Marine reports (1913 and 1923-24), the Coast Guard list, the Senate report's Appendix 4 table and witness list, the 2024 Coast Guard release, and secondary sources (LighthouseFriends, the Lighthouse Directory) for the 1927 beacon, the 1960 tower and the keeper list. The 1927 first light is not confirmed against a primary report: the local corpus of Marine reports stops at fiscal 1924, and the 1927-28 report was not found online. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts are restated in our words, with one short quotation, and the 1928 report is cited second-hand through it. The 1912-13 entry is confirmed on the corpus page (printed p. 52, scan p. 59). The 1923-24 casualty is printed p. 144 (scan p. 151) and dated 3 April 1923 on that page. The Nome Daily Nugget page (loc.gov, p. 2) was read directly. The 1937 Cordova item is distant (fifteen miles) and no source ties it to the station; the editor may drop it. Wikipedia gives 1957 for the lighthouse; it is a lead only and is not used. Keeper names after about 1960 come only from LighthouseFriends' list and the 2010 Senate witness list. Harvey Bergen's end date is 2013 in LighthouseFriends' list and 2012 in its text; the story states both. Eric Van Rooyen's keeper year is not printed; the 1995 date is taken from the December 1995 article in which he appears, and the story no longer dates his broadcasts. The Senate appendix table (Automated / Remote / Positions / Staffing columns) was read from the report's text layer, not an OCR scan, and the Bonilla row sits in the same column order as the rest of the table. Staffing after 2024 is not confirmed: the 2024 release does not name Bonilla. Shared names across LighthouseFriends lists (Richard Rose, Martin Mountford) appear at other BC stations; no link is made.
